title: A tweet claims a milestone shipped that's still open
author: off-by-one
description: Extracts every 'milestone #N' claim phrase (milestone_claims.py's shared grammar) from the connected X account's own tweets and checks the named milestone's real state. A milestone that exists but is still open is the seam: the tweet is a permanent public record claiming a bundle of work shipped that, in fact, never closed out. The tweet-side twin of release-claims-open-milestone (task 385), closing the milestone-claim half of the release-vs-tweet split tweet-claims-unmerged-pr and tweet-claims-unfixed-issue already opened for PR and issue claims.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the tweet's own created_at, mirroring release-claims-open-milestone's and tweet-claims-unfixed-issue's identical reasoning: a claim checked within 24 hours of the tweet might still be a race (posted moments before the milestone actually closes out) rather than a settled public overclaim (0.5, below the 0.70 bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden). Past 24 hours with the named milestone still open, it is unambiguous (flat 0.85 -- a posted tweet is as permanent and unedited as a published release body once the window passes; X carries no edit history the way a release body can be revised). A named milestone that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0 -- a broken reference is not this recipe's own seam. A named milestone that IS closed is excluded too, named not hidden -- the claim was true.
